races.title: State House, District 8
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Gloristine Brown
cands.bio: Democrat representing North Carolina House District 8 (Pitt County) since January 2023. Former nurse who also worked in insurance. Town board member in Bethel since 1999, mayor since 2014, and a Pitt Community College trustee. Holds a master of public administration from Strayer University.

endorsements.text: Sierra Club North Carolina is listed among her 2026 endorsements.

cands.gaps: We could not find her specific birthplace or hometown, or when or whether she lived outside North Carolina. We found no documented statements from her on data centers, development limits, homestead property taxes, out-of-state or institutional land buyers, immigration or H-1B, policing, gun laws, or school choice and teacher pay. We found no news coverage of controversies, and no information on foreign ties. She did not complete Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey in any year. The pages we had did not show which specific bills she sponsored, and the Wikipedia page was very brief.

local.label: Roots 100: Her campaign website describes her as an Eastern North Carolinian, born-and-raised, and she has served on the Bethel town board since 1999.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Prior legislative service in the NC House since 2023; Bethel town commissioner since 1999 and mayor since 2014; earlier work in nursing and insurance; master of public administration (Strayer, 2013).
qual.why: Legislative experience plus a long record in local elected office, including mayor, puts her in the upper-middle to high range. Her career was in nursing and insurance rather than law or budget work. Committee seats and her college trustee role were not counted.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: Her campaign site says she has supported legislation to restore protections to wetlands and other sensitive ecosystems.

prio.label: Matches 1 of 2 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 1 only promised

roots.summary: Her campaign website describes her as an Eastern North Carolinian, born-and-raised, and she has served on the Bethel town board since 1999.

cands.name: Cathy Thorne Bynum
cands.bio: Republican candidate for N.C. House District 8 in 2026. Born in Elm City, she earned a mechanical engineering degree from N.C. A&T, worked at Procter & Gamble, then taught high school math in Pitt County Schools for nearly two decades. She has held no elected office.
cands.gaps: We found no record of any elected office, bills, or official actions. Her campaign site mentions "tax relief" and "attracting business" only in general terms, with no specifics on property taxes, data centers, development, land ownership, immigration, policing, guns, abortion, or schools. She did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey. Her biography (birthplace, degree, years teaching, Teacher of the Year award, community work) comes only from her own campaign website, and we found no independent source to confirm it. We found no news coverage of her, and no information on when she began living in North Carolina beyond her account of growing up in Elm City.

local.label: Roots 100: Her campaign website says she was born in Elm City, NC, grew up there as the eighth of nine children, and later taught in Pitt County Schools for nearly two decades.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Mechanical engineering degree (N.C. A&T, 1980, Navy cooperative program), early career at Procter & Gamble, then nearly two decades as a high school math teacher in Pitt County Schools, including a Teacher of the Year honor at Farmville Central High School. She has held no elected office, and the site describes unspecified community initiatives.
qual.why: She has a real work history in engineering and teaching, but none in legislating, policy, budgeting, law, or elected office, so she falls in the low band for writing law and the state budget.
